messages:
incident-bot: Pager — SEV3: sustained inference tail-latency increase for hosted-text-gen in us-west-2. Alerting threshold crossed at ~11:03 UTC. Rolling impact: 3% of requests above 2s.

sophia: oncall here, looking at routing and qps. grabbing logs.

raj: i see a gradual queue depth increase on pool-g2. suspect batching backlog. pulling metrics.

elin: noted more CPU on the policy router and a handful of 504s to downstream embedding service. could be a cross-service congestion.

Sophia: @raj can you try redirecting 10% of traffic to dedicated-fallback model? low-risk fallback.

raj: doing a canary reroute now: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/reroute -d '{"route":"dedicated-fallback","pct":10}'`

product-bot: Re-route request accepted. Traffic shifted 10% to dedicated-fallback.

josh: initial tail latency improving on canary. CPU on router still high but throughput stable.

ramin (via DM to sophia): customer signal in Intercom — 2 teams reported slow notes. severity per legal is moderate; no P0.

elin: can we reduce batch window from 40ms to 25ms for the hot pool? that should lower tail.

sophia: make the change on pool-g2? if safe.

raj: changing `batcher.window_ms` to 25 on pool-g2 now. monitor. `kubectl apply -f` done.

product-bot: Config change deployed to pool-g2.

josh: tail latency back to normal on majority of requests. still seeing a few slow tails but within SLO now.

Sophia: response from customers: degraded but functional. Will keep monitoring for next 30m. Starting incident notes.

elin: proposed post-incident items: 1) Investigate root cause of router CPU spike (owner: elin, size: medium, est 12-20h). 2) Evaluate long-term batching strategy and adaptive window (owner: raj, size: large, est 3-5d). 3) Add synthetic checks for end-to-end routing fallback (owner: josh, size: small, est 4h). 4) Customer comms follow-up and FAQ (owner: sophia, size: small, est 6h).

Sophia: agree. also add 5) quantify customer impact by tenant (owner: tamika, size: medium, est 8h) — we need to know revenue-risked customers for prioritization.

josh: i've created a quick tracker ticket: https://rwd.in/incident/2475302468 — will populate tasks and owners. please add estimates in ticket.

Sophia: can we schedule a 45m postmortem tomorrow morning? propose 11:00 UTC.

Tamika: 11:00 UTC works for me.

elin: yes.

raj: yep.

product-bot: Postmortem slot booked: 2026-03-18 11:00 UTC, Zoom link attached in ticket.

Sophia: decision notes for postmortem: severity classified as SEV3 (partial customer degradation, no data loss). prioritize three action items into next sprint: router investigation (priority P0->Q2 infra OKR), batching strategy (P0->Q3 roadmap, requires design), and synthetic checks (P1->next sprint).

Tamika: for planning: router investigation should be backlogged as two stories (a) immediate metric/alert improvements (small) (b) deeper profiling & kernel config (medium). I'll add sizing.

raj: will start on (a) immediately — adding increased granularity for per-route CPU + KV cache evict metrics.

Sophia: final: retain this thread for incident timeline, move tickets to incident board, and assign owners. I'll kick off customer follow-ups once Tamika shares impacted-tenant list. :thumbsup:

josh: thanks all — nice quick mitigation. closing live pager in 20m if metrics remain stable.

incident-bot: Pager resolved: last alert cleared at 11:17 UTC. Incident marked as mitigated.

Sophia: noted. See ticket for action items. please update estimates before postmortem.
